title: Introducing the RevenueCat CLI
summary: Set up, manage, and run your app from the terminal. For you and your coding agent.
body_markdown:
RevenueCat should work wherever you build. For a growing number of you, and for your coding agents, that's the terminal.


Today we're releasing the[RevenueCat CLI](https://www.revenuecat.com/cli) . It brings the work you'd do in the dashboard, from setting up a new app to managing customers, into the terminal. The CLI joins the[AI Toolkit](https://www.revenuecat.com/feature/ai-toolkit) , RevenueCat's set of tools for working with AI agents.


Prefer to watch first? This is the CLI in action.


## Install


npm


```text
npm   install   -g   @revenuecat/cli
```


Homebrew (macOS / Linux)


```text
brew   install   RevenueCat/tap/rc
```


Then sign in with` rc auth login` , or create an account with` rc auth signup` if you don't have one yet.


## A few highlights


The commands below are a few of our favorites, not the full list.


### New app? One command sets it up


Run` rc setup` in your app's folder. It finds the coding agents installed on your machine, like Claude Code or Codex, and hands one of them the job of setting up RevenueCat for your app.


The agent creates the project, the products, an entitlement (what a purchase unlocks), an offering (what the paywall shows), a paywall, and the SDK integration, all in Test Store, RevenueCat's sandbox. When it's done, you can open the app, see the paywall, make a test purchase, and watch the entitlement unlock.


When you're ready for the App Store, one more command connects it:


```text
rc   setup   apple   app_x
```


It signs you in with your Apple Account, creates the App Store Connect API key and the in-app purchase key, and uploads both straight to RevenueCat.


### Sync products with the stores


A 'product' here refers to something a user can buy in your app, like a monthly or an annual subscription. Create them from the terminal and sync them to App Store Connect or Google Play.


```text
rc   products   create   --store-id   premium_annual   --type   subscription   \
--app-id   app_x   --title   "Premium Annual"   --duration   P1Y
rc   products   store   sync   app_x
```


` rc products store sync` creates and updates your products in App Store Connect or Google Play Console, so you never have to open either.


### Build a paywall from a prompt, then send Apple the screenshot


Describe the paywall you want and the CLI builds it with the RevenueCat Paywalls AI Editor. Attach a screenshot or a style guide to steer the design.


```text
rc   paywalls   generate   --prompt   "A calm annual-first paywall"
```


It creates a draft. Pass` --offering-id` to attach it to an offering. When the design is ready, hand Apple the screenshot App Review asks for.


```text
rc   products   store   screenshot   prod_abc   --file   paywall.png
```


The image goes straight to App Store Connect as the product's review screenshot.


### Manage customers


Look up a customer, give them access to a feature, refund a payment, or move their purchases to another account. All you need is their customer ID.


```text
rc   customers   show   cus_abc
rc   customers   grant   cus_abc   pro   --duration   monthly
rc   subscriptions   refund   sub_x
rc   customers   transfer   cus_old   --to   cus_new
```


` show` puts the customer, their subscriptions, and their purchases in one view.


When you need the dashboard anyway,` rc open customers cus_abc` jumps straight to that customer's page. Add` --print` to get the link without opening a browser, ready to drop into a support ticket or a Slack thread.


### Ask Rico from the terminal


Rico, RevenueCat's AI agent, answers questions about your metrics and configuration and can change your setup for you.


```text
rc   rico   "why did trial conversions drop this week?"
```


### Give your agent the skills


Skills are short playbooks that teach your coding agent how to work with RevenueCat.` rc skills install` adds them to Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and GitHub Copilot.


```text
rc   skills   install
```


## Built for you and your agent


In a terminal you get readable output. Add` --json` and the same command returns structured output an agent can parse. That includes the CLI itself. Ask it what it can do and it answers in JSON.


```text
rc   commands   --json
```


Every prompt is also a flag or an environment variable.` --json` returns a stable schema,` --format` trims the response to the fields an agent needs.


## Explore the other 150+ commands


These were a few of our favorites.` rc --help` lists every command group,` rc commands --json` prints the full tree, and the[command reference](https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/tools/cli/commands) in the docs covers each one.


There are commands for entitlements, offerings, experiments, charts, webhooks, and everything else in the dashboard.


For anything without a command yet,` rc api` sends a raw request to the v2 REST API with your credentials attached. The CLI talks to the same API as the dashboard, so anything you do in one shows up in the other.


## Install the CLI


```text
npm   install   -g   @revenuecat/cli
```


New app? Run` rc setup` . Existing app? Run` rc auth login` . The[docs](https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/tools/cli) cover every command, and the source is on[GitHub](https://github.com/RevenueCat/cli) , MIT licensed.
